item.text: I’m checking a few direct sources to verify the 2024 pattern on crisis handling, protest management, cabinet changes, and legal pressure, then I’ll synthesize the best claim-level evidence into a compact note.

item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mixed, leaning slightly positive on tactical adaptation and regime preservation. Tinubu repeatedly adjusted methods in 2024 when reforms, protests, or institutional bottlenecks threatened momentum, but he also leaned heavily on coercion and legal pressure against dissent, which helped immediate control while damaging longer-run legitimacy.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Nigeria Opens Land and Air Borders with Republic of Niger, Lift Other Sanctions](https://statehouse.gov.ng/nigeria-opens-land-and-air-borders-with-republic-of-niger-lift-other-sanctions/) | State House, Abuja | 2024-03-14 | Tinubu converted ECOWAS pressure into reintegration by lifting sanctions and reopening borders, showing he could switch from punishment to accommodation when that better served regional influence and stability. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.8

- [Nigeria restarts cash transfers to cushion hardship caused by reforms](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Nigeria-restarts-cash-transfers-to-cushion-hardship-caused-by-reforms-46031196/) | Reuters via MarketScreener | 2024-02-26 | The administration reallocated resources to vulnerable households after subsidy removal, a clear tactical adjustment meant to blunt backlash and keep the reform program politically viable. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.8, 8B.7

- [Tinubu establishes comprehensive economic coordination and planning system for Nigeria](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/) | State House, Abuja | 2024-03-27 | Tinubu created PECC/EET and put the finance minister, CBN governor, economists, and private-sector figures at the center of implementation, which is strong evidence of method adaptation and tighter control over execution. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.8

- [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/) | State House | 2024-08-04 | Tinubu publicly acknowledged deaths, destruction, and legitimate public frustration, then asked protesters to pause for dialogue and told law enforcement to protect lives and property responsibly. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.8, 8B.7

- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-07-31 | The government offered dialogue while security forces deployed in major cities, showing a mixed crisis posture that combined negotiation with coercive readiness rather than a clean restraint-first response. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.8

- [President Tinubu directs reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/) | State House, Abuja | 2024-06-15 | Tinubu used executive authority to reorder a core procurement gatekeeper for efficiency and transparency, which is a direct example of replacing or retooling an implementer to keep the program moving. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.8

- [Nigeria’s Tinubu names seven ministers, sacks five in cabinet reshuffle](https://theprint.in/world/nigerias-tinubu-names-seven-ministers-sacks-five-in-cabinet-reshuffle/2325625/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-10-23 | Tinubu reworked the cabinet, removed underperformers, and retained finance, defence, and planning, which looks like active executive performance management rather than paralysis. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.8

- [Tinubu orders probe of security agents involved in arrest, detention of minors](https://www.thecable.ng/tinubu-orders-probe-of-security-agents-involved-in-arrest-detention-of-minors/) | TheCable | 2024-11-04 | After backlash, Tinubu ordered an investigation into the detention and treatment of minors and said involved officers could face discipline, showing late but real corrective action after an abuse became politically costly. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 3B.4, 8B.8

- [Nigeria charges protesters with treason, inciting military](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-09-02 | The state escalated protest into treason and mutiny allegations, using criminal law to neutralize dissent rather than absorb it as normal political pressure. | Question IDs: 8B.9

- [Nigeria: Protesters Charged with Treason](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-06 | HRW said authorities held protesters, including children, in prolonged detention and used treason charges to signal intolerance for dissent, which undercuts any claim of durable, disciplined crisis management. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 3B.4

- [Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, and torture during the crackdown, showing that the state’s response preserved control through coercion rather than through a stable, legitimacy-preserving correction. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 3B.4, 8B.8

- [Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-10-03 | Even after reform, journalists were still prosecuted under the Cybercrimes Act for corruption reporting, indicating that the administration tolerated legal pressure on scrutiny instead of fully relaxing institutional resistance. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 7B.1, 8B.8

- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Freedom House found no internet shutdowns, which is a weak positive, but also said legal pressure and intimidation continued to chill journalists and activists, so the state did not fully normalize open contestation. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 7B.1, 8B.8

- [Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency](https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/) | BusinessDay | 2024-02-21 | The son-in-law appointment to the Federal Housing Authority is the clearest patronage signal in the 2024 record and cuts against any clean merit-only or institution-insulated reading. | Question IDs: 8B.9; also 8B.4

**Search Gap**  
I did not find a credible end-of-year source showing that the crackdown on protests, the treason cases, or the cybercrime pressure on journalists had been structurally reversed by December 2024. The strongest corrective moves were late, reactive, and partial, so the record supports adaptation under pressure, not durable restraint.
